label: Flooded area (Sentinel-1 radar)
aggregation: flooded share of known area x county area
notes: Radar (C-band SAR) change detection on a ~440 m grid (10 m scenes read at 160 m, block-averaged): a pixel is FLOODED when its monthly mean VV-VH ratio is > 3.0 dB above its own dry-season reference (median of the March means 2018-2025) - water under grass/papyrus/rice produces a double bounce that brightens VV much more than VH; OPEN WATER = VV < -18 and VH < -24 dB. Sees through cloud (unlike MODIS) and sees water under vegetation, which is most of the Sudd flood. It measures inundation BEYOND the normal dry-season state: permanent swamp is part of the reference and is not counted, so values are near 0 in the dry season. Validated on 4-8 Oct 2022 UNOSAT (new flood vs March 2022: F1 0.59, area ratio 0.95; see docs/CLIMATE_DATA_DECISIONS.md). Revisit 6-12 days 2018-2021, 12-24 days after Sentinel-1B failed (Dec 2021) until Sentinel-1C (2025): pixels without an acquisition inherit the previous month (max 2); county-months with <50% known area dropped. index_ok false: dry-season months and many 2018 months are ~0.
source: Copernicus Sentinel-1 A/B IW GRD, radiometrically terrain-corrected (sentinel-1-rtc) via Microsoft Planetary Computer
